ArtifactDate: c. 1st century BC - AD 70 (Second Temple steps)
CurrentLocation: In situ, City of David, Jerusalem, Israel
Description: The monumental stepped pool at the end of Hezekiah's Tunnel, rediscovered in 2004 when workers repairing a sewer line uncovered its broad stone steps. Excavation revealed a large Second Temple-period pool used by pilgrims ascending to the Temple.
BiblicalSignificance: In John 9, Jesus sends a man born blind to wash in Siloam, and he comes back seeing. Standing on these very steps, readers can trace that journey of faith, and remember that the One who opened blind eyes still opens ours to hope.
Interpretations: Scholars agree the stepped pool uncovered in 2004 is the Second Temple Pool of Siloam of John 9; its Hasmonean and Herodian phases show a large pilgrim facility, not a small spring.
